title: Vega GPU Systems - Redwood Partner Intro & Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood (AE + SE) and Vega GPU Systems to explore resell/co-sell partnership, technical integration options for dedicated and private deployments, and pilot benchmarking. Discussed typical enterprise asks (VPC peering, KMS, SOC 2), hardware compatibility (H100/A100), and a proposed pilot to run Redwood's inference workload on Vega infra. Agreed next steps: share partner deck/term sheet, schedule SE deep dive, exchange security docs, and set up pilot scope and timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to send partner deck + high-level partner term sheet (Lena) - by 2026-06-28
Schedule technical deep dive + benchmarking session with Vega infra team and Redwood SE (Ravi + Priya) - target week of 2026-07-06
Vega to share AWS/private cloud topology and available GPU SKUs, network details for VPC peering (Marta) - by 2026-06-30
Exchange security and compliance docs (SOC 2 report, SAML/SOAR details) and NDA if needed (Simon & Lena) - by 2026-06-29
action_items: Lena Ortiz: send partner deck, partner program overview, and sample term sheet - due 2026-06-28
Ravi Singh: prepare benchmark plan and list of test prompts + latency objectives for pilot - due 2026-07-02
Marta Alvarez: provide Vega GPU SKU list, networking diagram, and contact for infra onboarding - due 2026-06-30
transcript:
MEETING HEADER: Date: 2026-06-25; Start: 16:00 PDT; Duration: ~48 min; Recording: yes; Link: (redacted)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena with Redwood - I'm the AE on the partner program, uh we've got Ravi from our SE team here. quick intros?
[00:12] Marta Alvarez: Hi all, Marta here, head of partnerships at Vega. thanks for setting this up.
[00:16] Ethan Cole: Ethan, CTO. 
[00:19] Priya Nair: Priya, lead SE on infra.
[00:22] Simon Brooks: Simon, ops.
[00:25] Ravi Singh: great to meet you. quick agenda - intro, go-to-market intents, infra + integration surface, security checklist, and pilot idea.
[01:02] Lena Ortiz: high level - Redwood's partner program supports resell, co-sell and technical alliances. we want to understand where Vega thinks there's overlap; are you primarily selling hardware to enterprises, or pack infra + managed services?
[01:22] Marta Alvarez: mostly infra + managed services, we run private cloud in some regions, we also do on-prem racks for a few larger customers. we want to add value via software partnerships - so thinking of reseller or bring your own software.
[01:37] Ethan Cole: and from infra perspective we run mix of H100 and A100 nodes, some customers still on A100. network is peered into several customer VPCs, and we offer VPC peering or direct connect options.
[01:52] Ravi Singh: makes sense. from Redwood side, two common integrations: 1) we host via Redwood Dedicated on your hardware (we'd ship runtime or cooperate on deployment), 2) private deployment where customer runs Redwood in their VPC with our control-plane optional, and 3) marketplace listing for customers to spin up. each has different network and security touchpoints.
[02:22] Priya Nair: for private deployments we'd want to know the expected control-plane connectivity - do you need outbound to Redwood, or can everything be air-gapped?
[02:35] Lena Ortiz: we have both options. hosted control plane needs egress for telemetry and billing, but we can do an offline/air-gapped on-prem package for regulated customers. some details are in our partner deck, we'll share.
[02:50] Simon Brooks: on compliance - SOC 2 is typical ask, SAML/SSO for admins, KMS integration for customer keys. what's Redwood's posture?
[03:05] Ravi Singh: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SAML (Okta), and we support KMS integrations for key management; for private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and do audit logging. we'll share certs and the security pack.
[03:18] Marta Alvarez: good. on the business side, revenue split expectations?
[03:23] Lena Ortiz: we have a couple of partner tiers; typical resell uses a margin model + support credits; co-sell is commission-based. we can share a sample term sheet.
[03:37] Ethan Cole: technically, curious about runtime compatibility with your inference engine - do you require specific CUDA versions or driver stacks? sometimes our customers run mixed driver stacks and patching is painful.
[03:52] Ravi Singh: Redwood runtime works with standard CUDA drivers; H100 in particular we optimize with certain kernels - we usually certify driver + CUDA versions per SKU, and for mixed fleets we can run compatibility mode. for H100 we recommend CUDA 12.x and newest NCCL for multi-GPU.
[04:14] Priya Nair: latency targets? customers ask about p95 token latencies.
[04:19] Ravi Singh: depends on model and batch size. typical small Llama-like 13B low-latency profile p95 is sub-200ms for single-token under optimized runtime on H100; larger models go up. for production we suggest a pilot to run your workload and measure.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: sketching a pilot: Redwood provides benchmark script, a set of prompts, and expected SLOs; Vega runs on a representative infra and we compare tokens/sec, p50/p95 and cost.
[04:53] Marta Alvarez: acceptable. what's the scope - do you need raw access to machines or can we use a container runtime?
[04:59] Ravi Singh: container runtime is fine; we run in k8s or bare-metal containers. we just need GPU device access and network for telemetry if using hosted control plane.
[05:20] Simon Brooks: any custom licensing for runtime on customer infra?
[05:24] Lena Ortiz: we have enterprise licensing for private deployments (platform fee + support). reseller/marketplace routes are different - we'll send examples.
[05:38] Ethan Cole: security question - can audit logs be forwarded to customer's SIEM?
[05:41] Ravi Singh: yes, we can forward logs (structured) to S3, log collectors or SIEM via syslog/agents depending on deployment.
[05:55] Priya Nair: network egress - some customers disable egress entirely. for the offline package what capabilities are limited?
[06:02] Lena Ortiz: offline package supports inference runtime and local telemetry; advanced analytics and billing callbacks are limited; we provide a support channel and periodic syncs.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Marta Alvarez: earlier you mentioned marketplace - do you have existing cloud marketplace listings?
[06:27] Lena Ortiz: yes, Redwood's in a few marketplaces and has a private marketplace packaging capability for partners. we can support AMI/container images and onboarding docs.
[06:40] Ethan Cole: benchmark specifics - will you want full NVMe transfer speeds, interconnect metrics?
[06:45] Ravi Singh: ideally yes. for KV-cache heavy workloads we want PCIe/NVLink topology and perf on multi-GPU NCCL. we'll provide a checklist.
[06:58] Simon Brooks: competitors - customers sometimes ask to compare Lambda or Paperspace - how do you position versus them?
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: Redwood's differentiator is unified runtime + observability + routing across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; we focus on inference economics and predictable SLOs not just access to GPUs.
[07:20] Priya Nair: is there a preferred way to surface telemetry? Prometheus? traces?
[07:25] Ravi Singh: we expose metrics via Prometheus and traces via Jaeger-compatible collectors; logs in structured JSON to S3 or syslog.
[07:36] [00:07:36] Marta Alvarez: thinking about go-to-market, Vega could offer Redwood as an add-on managed stack to customers; we also can introduce Redwood in RFPs. we need pricing guidance to position.
[07:50] Lena Ortiz: we'll include partner pricing ranges in the deck; final pricing depends on committed capacity and support tier.
[08:02] Ethan Cole: on the pilot timeline - how long do you usually run benchmarks?
[08:06] Ravi Singh: typically 1-2 weeks of tests to stabilize numbers; 3-4 weeks if customers want long-run load tests. for this discovery we recommend a 2-week pilot.
[08:24] Priya Nair: ok. what's the onboarding friction - do you require specific kernel modules or can we run standard kernels?
[08:30] Ravi Singh: standard kernels are fine; we do recommend matching driver versions on nodes. if air-gapped we send packages with dependencies.
[08:45] [00:08:45] Simon Brooks: question on billing/usage - if we resell Redwood, is billing through Vega or direct to end-customer?
[08:52] Lena Ortiz: both models are possible; resell via Vega invoicing is supported for partners on the resell tier.
[09:03] Marta Alvarez: nice. any legal/contract pre-reqs?
[09:07] Lena Ortiz: NDAs are typical; we'll share partner legal checklist. Simon, you can coordinate on legal.
[09:15] Simon Brooks: will do.
[09:18] [00:09:18] Ethan Cole: technical deep dive might want to include multi-tenant isolation details if we host multiple customers on same hardware.
[09:26] Ravi Singh: we support tenant isolation via container-level RBAC and kv-cache namespace separation; for stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated pools per tenant.
[09:39] Priya Nair: good to know.
[09:45] Lena Ortiz: ok, quick recap so we're aligned: Redwood to send partner deck + term sheet; setup SE deep dive to scope pilot; Vega to provide topology and SKU list; exchange security docs - any other asks?
[10:00] Marta Alvarez: would like sample contract language for resell.
[10:04] Lena Ortiz: will include sample contract.
[10:08] Ethan Cole: for benchmarks, we'll want the exact prompt set and load generator.
[10:12] Ravi Singh: we'll provide the scripts and expected metrics list.
[10:18] [00:10:18] Simon Brooks: timeline review - if we get docs this week we can schedule the pilot for early July.
[10:24] Lena Ortiz: sounds good.
[10:28] Priya Nair: minor note - please include expected resource footprints per model size so we can size clusters.
[10:33] Ravi Singh: noted. we'll include CPU/GPU/memory and NVMe suggestions.
[10:40] Marta Alvarez: any red flags from Redwood's side about our network architecture?
[10:44] Ravi Singh: not yet; we'll review the topology you send and flag anything.
[10:48] [00:10:48] Lena Ortiz: we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the SE deep dive and share the deck. thanks everyone.

END OF TRANSCRIPT (truncated)

NOTES: Transcript includes occasional minor transcription errors; referred artifacts: partner_deck_v1.pdf (link), security_pack_redwood.zip (link), benchmark_script.tar.gz (link).
